pages.title: The need for quiet
pages.instruction: Read for the facts and the different priorities
pages.author: Home-working perspective · simulated source
pages.subject: Predictability, not silence at all costs
paragraphs: The person working at home says sound from late calls makes concentrated evening work difficult. The concern is not who the other person contacts; it is not knowing when the shared room will be quiet. A predictable period would make it easier to schedule demanding work. The person is willing to discuss exceptions but does not want every evening to require a new negotiation.

The account describes an impact, not proof that the caller is inconsiderate. An effective request needs a concrete time, a place or behaviour that can change, and a way to review the arrangement. A judgement about personality is less actionable than a description of when concentration is interrupted.

pages.title: The need for contact
pages.instruction: Read for the facts and the different priorities
pages.author: Family-call perspective · simulated source
pages.subject: A different time zone
paragraphs: The other person uses late calls to stay in touch with family in a different time zone. An earlier routine slot is not always available. They are willing to use a smaller room and headphones, but worry that an absolute ban would also prevent an urgent conversation. They want a clear difference between a regular arrangement and an exceptional situation.

This perspective does not remove the impact of sound in a shared space. It identifies a second need that a workable agreement must address. Both people could benefit from naming an ordinary quiet period and agreeing how to communicate an exception, rather than treating every deviation as proof of bad intentions.

pages.title: Raise the impact, not an accusation
pages.instruction: Listen for the problem, the response and the next step

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Could we bring up the late calls before it becomes a recurring argument?
lines.audioText: Could we bring up the late calls before it becomes a recurring argument?
lines.translation: Podemos conversar sobre as ligações tarde antes de isso virar uma discussão recorrente?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Yes. I’ve been finding it difficult to concentrate when calls carry through the shared room
lines.audioText: Yes. I’ve been finding it difficult to concentrate when calls carry through the shared room.
lines.translation: Sim. Tenho achado difícil me concentrar quando o som das chamadas passa pela sala compartilhada

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: I understand. I’m calling family in another time zone, so an earlier slot is difficult
lines.audioText: I understand. I’m calling family in another time zone, so an earlier slot is difficult.
lines.translation: Entendo. Ligo para a família em outro fuso, então um horário mais cedo é difícil

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Would you mind using the smaller room and headphones after nine?
lines.audioText: Would you mind using the smaller room and headphones after nine?
lines.translation: Você se importaria de usar o quarto menor e fones depois das nove?

questions.prompt: Why can’t the calls simply move much earlier?

pages.title: Protect both interests
pages.instruction: Listen for the problem, the response and the next step

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: I can do that, but I wouldn’t want to promise there will never be an urgent call
lines.audioText: I can do that, but I wouldn’t want to promise there will never be an urgent call.
lines.translation: Posso fazer isso, mas não gostaria de prometer que nunca haverá uma ligação urgente

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: That’s reasonable. I’d rather you let me know when there’s an exception than leave me guessing
lines.audioText: That’s reasonable. I’d rather you let me know when there’s an exception than leave me guessing.
lines.translation: É razoável. Eu preferiria que me avisasse quando houvesse uma exceção em vez de me deixar adivinhar

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Could we agree a regular quiet period, with a brief message if something unusual happens?
lines.audioText: Could we agree a regular quiet period, with a brief message if something unusual happens?
lines.translation: Podemos combinar um período de silêncio, com uma mensagem breve se algo incomum acontecer?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Yes. The main issue for me is predictable concentration time, not controlling who you speak to
lines.audioText: Yes. The main issue for me is predictable concentration time, not controlling who you speak to.
lines.translation: Sim. O principal para mim é ter um horário previsível de concentração, não controlar com quem você fala

questions.prompt: What is the quiet worker’s underlying need?

pages.title: Check the extent of agreement
pages.instruction: Listen for the problem, the response and the next step

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Then perhaps we can protect that time and still make the family call possible
lines.audioText: Then perhaps we can protect that time and still make the family call possible.
lines.translation: Então talvez possamos proteger esse horário e manter a ligação com a família

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: What period would be workable for you?
lines.audioText: What period would be workable for you?
lines.translation: Qual período seria viável para você?

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: I’ll check the family’s availability before committing to a precise end time
lines.audioText: I’ll check the family’s availability before committing to a precise end time.
lines.translation: Vou conferir a disponibilidade da família antes de me comprometer com um horário exato

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Thanks. Let’s confirm the arrangement rather than assume a polite response means full agreement
lines.audioText: Thanks. Let’s confirm the arrangement rather than assume a polite response means full agreement.
lines.translation: Obrigada. Vamos confirmar o acordo em vez de presumir que uma resposta educada significa concordância total

pages.title: Agree on a boundary
pages.instruction: Raise the issue and try to agree on a workable boundary

pages.title: A conditional agreement
pages.instruction: Listen for the new information and decide how to respond
pages.message: Hi, Ana. I can make the regular family call before ten thirty, using the smaller room and headphones. I’m willing to keep the shared room quiet after nine, provided we allow a brief exception for an urgent call and I message you if that happens. I’m not asking for unlimited late calls; I just don’t want us to treat an emergency as a broken routine agreement. Could you tell me whether that protects the concentration time you need? If the sound still carries, we can review the room arrangement rather than turn it into a judgement about either person’s consideration for others
pages.audioText: Hi, Ana. I can make the regular family call before ten thirty, using the smaller room and headphones. I’m willing to keep the shared room quiet after nine, provided we allow a brief exception for an urgent call and I message you if that happens. I’m not asking for unlimited late calls; I just don’t want us to treat an emergency as a broken routine agreement. Could you tell me whether that protects the concentration time you need? If the sound still carries, we can review the room arrangement rather than turn it into a judgement about either person’s consideration for others.
